doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Illness, cancer treatment and get-well poems
summary: Sherman and his wife Betty both faced serious illness; the band sent a cheap card, he answered with a poem, and he recovered through beam radiation.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Do you happen to have this poem memorized?
No I don’t believe I do.
Oh, well we’ll just have to do Interview Part II then where we’ll feature a reading.

Yeah. But any subject. Even bad health. My wife and I underwent serious illnesses at the very end of last year and the beginning of this one. She had two congestive heart failure attacks, hospitalized, quadruple bypass. The same day that she had quadruple bypass I was diagnosed with prostate cancer. So it was not a happy day. And the men in the Alumni All-Stars sent us flowers and a get well card. And the get well card, being cheap, it didn’t say to Dick or to Betty, it said “Get Well Quick.” So I sent them a poem chiding them for their cheapness and saying “you could have at least specified a name or two.” So I ended up, that one I can recall, I ended up saying — well I claim that I can remember it — I can’t. Well I’ll think about it and get back to it later.
Well it will come to you.
And we’ll revisit that. Well you are feeling better now, you look great.

Yeah. I recovered by means of radiation treatment. And it was not the seed implants, it was the beam radiation. A doctor introduced himself to me at the South Side Hospital where I went 38 times, every day, five days a week. You lie on an MRI type bed and this thing is beamed at you, and he introduced himself as the guy that was handling the beam, and I said, “I hope it’s not Jim Beam.” And he said, “No, no, no I’m usually off on the bourbon when I’m directing the treatment.” Anyway I’m pretty good now. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
